key_insight: Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA) lets attention heads read KV pairs from the current layer and from previous layers, preserving informative shallow-layer signals so they aren't lost as models get deeper.
problem_solved: Addresses signal degradation in very deep LLMs, where features formed in early layers are progressively diluted by repeated residual updates and become hard to recover in later layers.
method: Per-head mixture mechanism: each attention head attends to both current-layer KV pairs and depth KV pairs from preceding layers.
Learned or parameterized mixing across depths so heads can select/use the most informative layer-wise representations.
Design and optimizations for a hardware-efficient implementation to limit added compute and memory overhead.
impact: Enables deeper transformer models to retain and reuse early-layer features, improving scalability and robustness of deep LLMs while keeping computational costs manageable for practitioners.
visual_elements: Schematic of a transformer block showing an attention head attending to KV pairs from multiple previous layers (color-coded depth channels).
Line chart comparing performance or signal retention vs. model depth: baseline (signal decay) vs. MoDA (preserved signal).
Before/after diagram: residual-only propagation (dilution) vs. MoDA (direct multi-depth access).
Icon set: head-level gating (per-head selection), low-overhead hardware/efficiency badge, depth-stack illustration.
paper_authors: Lianghui Zhu, Yuxin Fang, Bencheng Liao, Shijie Wang, Tianheng Cheng
